event: A viral video, a news story or an Apple feature sends thousands of shoppers at once and the one Node process on the MacBook Air runs out of room, so answers slow down or stop.
trigger: A creator video, a news item, an Apple editorial feature or a campus craze (Canadian-only, so the whole spike lands on one server).
cost: Lost first impressions at the best moment: every shopper who sees a spinner or 'I need a connection' on day one is a lost Plus buyer and a likely 1-star review. Size: assumed ceiling of roughly 100 to 300 scans a second, about 1,000 to 2,000 shoppers in the same minute, so a day of 20,000 or more active users with an evening peak would pass it.
detect: Only the GitHub probe every 30 minutes (two misses in a row to email, so 30 to 60+ minutes late) and it passes on any answer inside 20 seconds, so a slow server does not alarm; otherwise a 1-star review.
response: 1. Check the Mac is up and the tunnel is connected. 2. Turn the paid features down first (raise nothing, drop Claude asks, drop usage-event upload). 3. Restart the server only if it is stuck, since a restart forgets every per-address count. 4. Post a one-line status in the app store notes only if it lasts hours.
smallest_fix: Run one load test against the real Mac with a script that imitates 500 and then 2,000 phones (scan, price, usage events), write down the number where answers pass 2 seconds, and write a five-line spike playbook beside it.
fix_cost: 2 to 3 hours, no money (free load tool)
sources: app/server.ts:122-125 (barcode lookup 0.2 ms on the main thread, sync sqlite); app/server.ts:636 (text search 24 to 113 ms, 735 ms vector arm, measured); no load test found in bench/ (it holds price accuracy tests) or app/test; .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml (30 min probe, retry once after 90 s); scripts/phone-contract-probe.mjs:127 (20 s timeout, no speed threshold); the 100 to 300 a second and 1,000 to 2,000 shoppers figures are assumed, not measured

event: Under heavy use the server's database writes (scan rows, usage events, a 200-event batch from a phone coming back online) all run one at a time on the main thread, and the nightly backup or weekly price refresh overlaps, so some scans or events are dropped.
trigger: A spike of scans plus many phones flushing queued usage events, or the 04:00 backup and Sunday 05:30 refresh landing on a busy night.
cost: Dropped scan rows undercount the weekly free scans (free users get extra scans, small revenue leak) and lose usage data. Size: assumed 1 to 5 ms per write, so a 200-event batch holds the whole server for about 0.2 to 1 second.
detect: Counted in memory as 'dropped' on the scan store; whether /api/health shows that count was not checked; nobody reads the server log.
response: 1. Look at the server log and health page for 'database is locked' or dropped counts. 2. Move the backup and refresh to a quieter hour. 3. Restart if the log shows the scan store handle gone.
smallest_fix: Write all events of one batch in one transaction, and add the dropped-scan count to the health check the 30 minute alarm already reads.
sources: app/src/scans.ts:183-215 (one handle, WAL, busy_timeout 5000, a failure is counted and never thrown, no synchronous pragma set so the sqlite default applies); app/server.ts:2020 (200 events per batch) and :4094-4120 (one insert per event); mac/launchd/com.shin.backup.plist:41-46 (04:00); mac/launchd/com.shin.hammer.plist:49-56 (Sunday 05:30); per-write millisecond figures assumed

event: A campus, a store's Wi-Fi or a carrier's shared address is counted as one person, so after about 15 phones on it the server answers every one of them 'That is a lot of requests, try again in a few minutes'.
trigger: A viral moment inside a university, a lecture hall, a grocery store with guest Wi-Fi, or a carrier that puts many phones behind one address.
cost: Lost conversions and 1-star reviews from the exact group that is spreading the app. Size: the door allows 1,200 requests per 10 minutes per address (120 a minute); a phone in use sends about 6 to 12 a minute (assumed), so about 10 to 20 phones at once fill it; paid-call windows are only 90 per 10 minutes and 600 a day per address.
detect: Nobody would know; the refusals are 429s in the access log that no alarm reads.
response: 1. Count 429s by address in the access log. 2. Raise SHIN_RATE_DOOR_IP_PER_10MIN and the per-address windows in the Mac config. 3. Restart the server (counts reset).
smallest_fix: Raise the door limit about five times (it only stops a flood) and count by device id as well as address; add a daily 429 count to the health check.
sources: app/src/rate-limit.ts:103-126 (door 1,200 per 10 min and 15,000 a day, address 90 per 10 min and 600 a day); app/src/rate-limit.ts:165 (the address is the exact Cloudflare header); app/server.ts:984-990 and :2480-2500 (door refusal answers 429); app/public/js/api.js:438 (phone shows 'rate_limited'); requests per phone and the shared-address behaviour of Canadian carriers and campuses are assumed

event: Once the weekly free limit is switched on, the free scans per address cap (30 a day) refuses new shoppers who share a campus, store or carrier address after only a few scans each.
trigger: The weekly limits go on at paid launch (they were off on 2026-11-16) and a group of friends or a campus adopts the app together.
cost: The cap fires on the third or fourth new user at one address, so first-time shoppers see a refusal on scan 1 to 10 and never reach a paywall; lost Plus sales and reviews. Size: 30 scans a day per address against 10 free a week per phone.
detect: Nobody would know; it is a 429 with the same text as any flood refusal.
response: 1. Count 429s on barcode scans per address in the access log. 2. Raise SHIN_FREE_SCANS_PER_IP_DAY (and restart). 3. Keep the 10-a-week device limit as the real gate.
smallest_fix: Raise the address cap to about 150 a day (it exists only so a made-up device id cannot reset the week), and show the shopper the paywall, not the 'lots of lookups' text, when the cap fires.
sources: app/src/rate-limit.ts:126-128 (30 a day); app/server.ts:995-1001 (only while the free limit is on, Plus exempt); app/server.ts:3136-3139 (refusal is the 429 text); docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:43 (C1, limits off); docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:77 (limits not set); whether they are still off now is assumed

event: When more shoppers use the app than the server can ask RevenueCat about (over 120 asks a minute), paying Plus subscribers are treated as free users and shown the paywall or a refusal.
trigger: A spike of a thousand or more different phones in ten minutes, each needing an answer to 'is this phone Plus?'.
cost: A subscriber who paid CA$3.99 or CA$29.99 is told to pay again: refund requests, cancellations, 1-star reviews. Size: 120 asks a minute with a ten-minute answer cache, about 1,200 different phones per ten minutes, each answered from the last known answer or 'not Plus' when over it.
detect: One warning line in the server log, at most once a minute; nobody reads it.
response: 1. Look for the '[plus-lookup-limit]' warning in the Mac log. 2. Raise the ceiling in code only after RevenueCat says its own limit allows it. 3. Tell subscribers who write in to restart the app (the 10 minute cache clears).
smallest_fix: Remember 'Plus' for a day (not ten minutes) once RevenueCat has said yes, so a subscriber is looked up once a day, and email the warning through the health check.
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:49 and :54 (ten minute cache, 120 a minute valve); app/src/scan-quota.ts:196-205 (over the valve: last known answer or false); app/server.ts:995-1000 (free-scan check asks for every barcode request while the limit is on); RevenueCat's own rate limit not checked

event: A shopper hits the free limit, buys Plus, and the server keeps saying 'not Plus' for up to ten minutes, so the scan after payment shows the paywall again.
trigger: Every normal first purchase: the server looked up the phone when the limit was hit and remembered 'not Plus' for ten minutes, and nothing clears that when the purchase completes.
cost: The moment of payment is the worst moment to fail: refund requests through Apple, 1-star reviews ('I paid and it still asks me to pay'), support emails. Size: affects every buyer who bought right after hitting the limit, which is the main path.
detect: Nobody would know until a review or an email; no check buys Plus and scans.
response: 1. Tell the writer to wait ten minutes or restart the server's entitlement check (restart clears it). 2. Fix the cache so a purchase clears it. 3. Refund only through Apple as the support page says.
smallest_fix: After a purchase, the app calls a small server route that drops that phone's cached answer, or the server remembers 'not Plus' for only 30 seconds.
fix_cost: 1 to 2 hours, no money; then one real sandbox purchase to see it work
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:49 (ten minute cache), :194-195 and :213 (a no is cached for ten minutes), :271-275 (checked only after the limit is reached); no cache clear found in app/src or app/server.ts (grep entitlementCache); app/public/js/purchases.js:208 (the phone remembers Plus locally only); the server path not run against a real purchase (not tested)

event: A spike uses up the 1,000-a-month Claude allowance in hours, and for the rest of the month shoppers whose product has no shop price get 'No price here yet' instead of an estimate.
trigger: A few thousand new shoppers scanning products Pexi has no price for; about 73 percent of scans had no shop price in the early data (27 percent had one).
cost: The estimate is what makes an unknown product still useful, so the shopper finds a dead end and does not return or pay. Money is small (about 0.2 to 0.3 cents a call, so 1,000 calls is a few dollars); the cost is answers. Size: 5,000 new shoppers with 5 unpriced scans each is 25,000 asks, 25 times the cap (assumed), so it would pass in hours.
detect: A log line (at most once an hour), a counted fault and a field on the health page; nobody reads them and the GitHub alarm does not read that field.
response: 1. Open the health page and read the Claude cap field. 2. Raise SHIN_RANGE_ASK_MONTHLY_CAP in the Mac config and restart. 3. Check the Anthropic account has credit.
smallest_fix: Make the 30 minute alarm email when the health page says the Claude cap is reached, and decide the ceiling in advance (for example 10,000 a month, a few tens of dollars).
fix_cost: 1 hour for the alarm line, plus Jamin's number; the extra Claude cost is about CA$20 a month at 10,000 calls (assumed from the identification price)
sources: identify/src/range-ask.ts:208 (cap 1,000) and :210 (90 day cache per item); app/server.ts:1657-1675 (loud log once an hour, health field); app/server.ts:1627-1650 (device 12 per 10 min and 40 a day, network 100 and 250); .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml (probe and price freshness only); NOW.md:149 (27 percent of 176 scans had a shop price); app/src/model-cost.ts:22 (0.23 cents is an identification price, a range ask is assumed similar); whether the range ask is on in production was not checked

event: With more than 5,000 different phones or addresses in a day, the in-memory limiters start forgetting the oldest ones, so the per-phone and per-address limits quietly weaken.
trigger: Real daily growth past about 5,000 distinct phones or addresses.
cost: More Claude asks than intended, up to the monthly cap, which bounds it: about CA$2 to CA$3 per 1,000 asks (assumed). It also lets one address use more than its 30 free scans once its record is forgotten. The cost is named and small.
detect: Nobody would know; it is by design and silent.
response: 1. Nothing urgent: the monthly Claude cap is the backstop. 2. If abuse shows up, raise the ceiling in rate-limit.ts or keep counts in the database.
smallest_fix: Write one line in RULINGS that Jamin accepts this at the cost of the Claude cap, or raise the ceiling to 100,000 keys (small memory).
fix_cost: 10 minutes to write the line, or 1 hour to change the ceiling; no money
sources: app/src/rate-limit.ts:33 (5,000 keys) and :74-90 (oldest-entered keys dropped past the ceiling); app/server.ts:1624-1625 (device and network limiters); RULINGS.md not checked for an existing acceptance

event: A spread-out national spike means thousands of different map squares, and the shop-lookup cache (500 squares, no sharing of a lookup already in flight) sends a flood of requests to the free public Overpass server, which then refuses or slows them.
trigger: Hundreds of shoppers in many cities at once, each opening the store picker; or a few shoppers in a dense area asking the same new square at the same moment.
cost: The store picker comes back empty (never an error), so shoppers type prices without a shop and the price data loses its store tag; a volunteer-run service may also block the Mac's address (the Mac loses the lookup, the rest of the app is untouched). Size: one lookup per new square per day, capped at 30 per 10 minutes and 300 a day per address.
detect: A log line 'the shop lookup did not answer'; nobody reads it; shoppers just see no shops.
response: 1. Check the server log for the Overpass line. 2. Switch SHIN_OVERPASS to another public mirror in the Mac config. 3. Restart.
smallest_fix: Share one lookup among simultaneous askers of the same square, raise the 500-square cache to several thousand, keep a failed square empty for an hour, and set a contact in the request header as Overpass asks.
sources: app/src/stores.ts:302-322 (10 second timeout, user agent 'shin-beta (price scanner, six testers)'); app/src/stores.ts:338-340 (day cache, 5 minute empty cache, 500 squares); app/src/stores.ts:362-390 (no in-flight map, failures return an empty list); app/server.ts:924 and :4144-4155 (30 per 10 min and 300 a day per address); Overpass's own fair-use limits not looked up (assumed)

event: Many Plus purchases arrive and the money, the payouts and the sales-tax threshold become real business tasks nobody has scheduled.
trigger: Plus sells (CA$3.99 a month, CA$29.99 a year); about 300 subscribers is roughly CA$1,200 a month before Apple's cut (assumed).
cost: A missed registration or filing means a fine and interest (CRA, assumed); the usual line is a GST/HST number once taxable sales pass CA$30,000 in four quarters (assumed from general knowledge, not checked in this pass); Apple already collects tax in some cases (see the finding). Also nobody watches renewals, refunds or chargebacks.
detect: The RevenueCat dashboard and App Store Connect sales page, if Jamin opens them; no alert.
response: 1. Look at the sales report monthly. 2. Ask CRA's business line (free) about GST/HST and the Apple election when sales approach CA$30,000. 3. Keep the Apple tax forms current.
smallest_fix: Put a monthly 10 minute 'money check' on Jamin's calendar: sales, refunds, the running total against CA$30,000, and a note of the day the GST/HST question gets asked.
fix_cost: 20 minutes to set up, no money

event: People outside Canada install the app, because the store availability is wider than Canada or a traveller carries it abroad, and get no prices, 1-star reviews and foreign subscriptions.
trigger: App Store availability still set to 148 countries (as of 2026-11-07), a foreign creator, or a Canadian travelling.
cost: Reviews from other storefronts say 'does not work in my country'; subscriptions sold in other currencies and tax regimes Pexi was not set up for. Size: assumed small at first, but a viral video is not stopped by a border.

response: 1. Open App Store Connect availability and confirm it is Canada only. 2. If foreigners already subscribed, refund them through Apple and remove the countries. 3. Reply to the reviews.

event: Support emails (how do I cancel, I paid and it is still limited, wrong price, delete my data) grow beyond what Jamin and Aurik can answer, and a data request goes past its 30 day clock in the pile.
trigger: Any real user base; a spike or a press mention multiplies it.
cost: Unanswered email becomes refunds, 1-star reviews and, for a data request, a missed 30 day legal deadline (Quebec and federal rules, per the data-requests doc). Size: assumed 1 to 3 emails per 100 users a month; at 10,000 users that is 100 to 300 a month.
detect: Nobody would know: who reads the inbox is not recorded, and the address still carries the old 'Shin' name.
response: 1. One of Jamin or Aurik reads the inbox once a day. 2. Send canned replies for cancel (Apple), refund (Apple), delete data (the data-request steps) and wrong price. 3. Log any data request with its date.

event: A journalist, a podcaster or a creator asks Pexi for a comment, an interview or a demo and nobody knows who answers or what is said.
trigger: A viral post, a local-news piece on grocery prices, or a creator wanting a free Plus code or a walkthrough.
cost: A fast good answer is free marketing (a feature is often worth more than any ad); a slow or off-message answer, or a story that quotes the old 'Shin' address or a wrong claim, costs the moment. Size: one inquiry can be thousands of installs.
detect: An email or a DM to the founder or the support inbox; nothing flags it as press.
response: 1. Reply within a day with a one-paragraph note. 2. Offer a TestFlight link or an Apple offer code for Plus. 3. Do not promise income or savings numbers.
smallest_fix: Write a one-page press note (what Pexi is, three facts, the support address, a photo of the screens, the founder's line) and prepare a batch of Apple offer codes for creators.
sources: docs/store/privacy.html names Jamin as contact; BRIEF.md (support address carries the old name); docs/store/screenshots (screens exist); no press or media page found in docs/store or docs

event: A retailer or brand asks to partner, advertise in the app or license the price data, and the public privacy policy already says 'no ads' and 'no selling data', so any yes makes the policy false.
trigger: A grocery chain, a brand or a data company notices Pexi's traffic or its price answers.
cost: If a yes goes out without updating the policy and the App Store privacy answers, the policy becomes untrue (an App Review problem and a Quebec and federal privacy complaint risk); a clumsy no loses a possible paying partner. Size: a single deal could be worth more than a year of subscriptions.
detect: An email to the support address or a message to the founder.
response: 1. Reply politely that Jamin will get back in a week. 2. Decide: no, not now, or yes with the policy and store answers changed first. 3. Never share per-phone data.
response_exists: yes: docs/store/privacy.html:43 and :82 (the stated position); no written reply or decision rule
smallest_fix: Write the standing answer ('not now, we will keep your note') and the three questions to ask any partner (what they want, what data moves, who pays), in a short file.
sources: docs/store/privacy.html:43 (no ads, no analytics companies), :82 (does not sell data or share with advertisers or data brokers); docs/store/terms.html:46 (not affiliated with any store); data-source terms are not covered here by instruction

event: As price rows pile up, a typed-name search that reads the whole price table on the main thread takes seconds and freezes the app for everyone while it runs.
trigger: The weekly price refresh adds rows every week (about 99,000 prices at first load); shoppers type product names.
cost: A frozen server for every shopper for the length of each typed search (see success-01). Size: assumed linear scan of about 100,000 rows takes tens of milliseconds today; if each refresh appends rows (the key includes the date), about 5 million rows in a year would take a second or two per search, assumed.
detect: Nobody would know; the 30 minute probe does not time searches and the latency report is admin only.
response: 1. Check the admin latency report for slow typed searches. 2. Run the price table's size query. 3. Add an index or move the search to a worker.
smallest_fix: Time one typed search against a copy of the Mac's price table at 1 million and 5 million rows, and move it to the search worker or add a name index if it passes 200 ms.

event: With real traffic, the request log, scan tables and 14 nightly backups on the same disk grow until the Mac's disk fills, and the server stops writing scans.
trigger: About 10,000 daily users, or less with a spike; the log keeps 90 days and the backup keeps 14 copies on the same disk.
cost: A full disk makes scans and events fail to save (the server swallows the error), backups fail, and the server can crash on startup. Size: each request writes a 281-byte log line (measured on the PC copy); 1.5 million requests a day is about 420 MB a day, about 38 GB over 90 days, against the 38 GiB free reported on 2026-11-07, assumed.
detect: Nobody would know; a disk guard stops writing pictures below 2 GB free but nothing alarms.
response: 1. Look at free disk on the Mac. 2. Shorten log retention or delete old backups. 3. Restart the server after space is back.
smallest_fix: Add free disk space to the health check and the 30 minute alarm (email below 10 GB), and compress or shorten the request log.

event: The Mac's home connection or the fanless Air itself becomes the limit under sustained load: the CPU slows down when hot and the home upload is shared with the household, and the tunnel carries everything.
trigger: A multi-hour spike; a household member on video calls; summer heat.
cost: Answers slow or drop with no error to find; the free Cloudflare plan is not the limit (assumed: no bandwidth bill), the Air is. Size: the app's answers are small (a few KB), so 300 a second is about 10 to 20 Mbit/s upload, assumed against an unknown home uplink.
detect: Nobody would know; no CPU, temperature or bandwidth alarm.
response: 1. Check the Mac's activity monitor and the tunnel's connection count. 2. Stop the weekly refresh and backup during the spike. 3. Move the server to a hosted machine if spikes repeat.
smallest_fix: Measure the home uplink once and note it in the playbook; decide in advance the number of daily users at which the server moves off the Air.
fix_cost: 30 minutes, no money (a small hosted machine would be about CA$10 to CA$30 a month, assumed)
sources: mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist (one server process, launchd keep-alive); mac/launchd/com.shin.tunnel.plist (cloudflared); mac/06-verify-no-sleep.sh (never sleeps on power); the Mac model, its RAM and the home uplink are not recorded in the repo (not found); free-plan behaviour assumed
